Practice Questions
Answer each question, then check the Hint and Solution tabs if you need help. Use the buttons below the questions to move between them, then press Submit when you’re done.



Question 1 of 4

QuestionHintSolution


Which of the following equations correctly model the relationship between a circle’s Area \(A\) and Radius \(r\) ?  (more than one correct choice)


 A. \(A = (\pi r)^2\)  B. \(\frac{A}{r}=\pi r\)  C. \(A=\pi^2 r\)  D. \(A = \pi r^2\)









TipHint 1





Demo of math diagrams










TipHint 2











Answer: B & D.  B:  \[
\begin{aligned}
    \frac{A}{r}&=\pi r \\
    r*\frac{A}{r}&=\pi r * r \\
    A&=\pi r^2 \\
\end{aligned}
\]





Question 2 of 4

QuestionHintSolution


A circle has radius \(r\) and diameter \(d\). Which of the following equations correctly relate \(r\) and \(d\)?  (more than one correct choice)

 A. \(d = \frac{r}{2}\)  B. \(r = \frac{d}{2}\)  C. \(r = 2d\)  D. \(d = 2r\)









TipHint 1





The diameter goes all the way across the circle through the center, so it’s made of two radii placed end to end.










TipHint 2





Which is bigger, \(d\) or \(r\)? An equation that makes the bigger one come out smaller is written backwards. Test each choice with a real number, like \(r = 3\) (so \(d = 6\)).





Answer: B & D.  Two radii make one diameter: \[
\begin{aligned}
    d &= r + r = 2r \\
    \frac{d}{2} &= r
\end{aligned}
\]
Why the others are wrong: A and C put the 2 on the wrong side. With \(r = 3\): choice A gives \(d = 1.5\) and choice C gives \(r = 12\) when \(d = 6\). In both cases the diameter comes out shorter than the radius, which can’t happen.





Question 3 of 4

QuestionHintSolution


Which of the following equations correctly give the circumference \(C\) of a circle with radius \(r\) and diameter \(d\)?  (more than one correct choice)

 A. \(C = 2\pi r\)  B. \(C = \pi r^2\)  C. \(C = \pi d\)  D. \(C = 2\pi d\)









TipHint 1





Circumference is a length: the distance around the circle. If you cut the circle and unroll it, its edge is a little more than 3 diameters long. That “little more than 3” is \(\pi \approx 3.14\).










TipHint 2





Since \(d = 2r\), try replacing \(d\) with \(2r\) in one choice and see whether it turns into another choice.  Also, a formula with \(r^2\) gives square units (like ft²), which measures area, not length.





Answer: A & C.  C is the definition of \(\pi\): the circumference is \(\pi\) diameters long. Substituting \(d = 2r\) gives A: \[
\begin{aligned}
    C &= \pi d \\
      &= \pi (2r) \\
      &= 2\pi r
\end{aligned}
\]
Why the others are wrong:

B (\(\pi r^2\)) is the area formula. It’s the most common mix-up on the ACT.
D (\(2\pi d\)) uses the “2” twice. Since \(d\) already equals \(2r\), \(2\pi d = 4\pi r\), which is double the real circumference.






Question 4 of 4

QuestionHintSolution


Which of the following equations correctly give the area \(A\) of a circle in terms of its diameter \(d\)?  (more than one correct choice)

 A. \(A = \pi d^2\)  B. \(A = \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2\)  C. \(A = \frac{\pi d^2}{2}\)  D. \(A = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}\)









TipHint 1





The area formula you know uses the radius: \(A = \pi r^2\). What do you replace \(r\) with if you only know \(d\)?









TipHint 2





A \(d \times d\) square around the circle splits into four \(r \times r\) squares.

When you square a fraction, square the top and the bottom: \(\left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 = \frac{d^2}{2^2}\).





Answer: B & D.  Replace \(r\) with \(\frac{d}{2}\): \[
\begin{aligned}
    A &= \pi r^2 \\
      &= \pi \left(\frac{d}{2}\right)^2 \\
      &= \pi \cdot \frac{d^2}{4} = \frac{\pi d^2}{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
Why the others are wrong:

A uses the diameter as if it were the radius. That’s 4 times too big.
C squares the \(d\) but forgets to square the 2. That’s 2 times too big.

Memory Match



Memory Match 1 of 2: Circle Formulas

QuestionHintSolution


Flip two cards at a time. Match each formula name to its formula.

memory([
  ["Area of a circle",     "A = \\pi r^2"],
  ["Circumference",        "C = 2\\pi r"],
  ["Diameter",             "d = 2r"],
  ["Equation of a circle", "(x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2"]
])














TipHint 1





Area is measured in square units, so its formula squares the radius: \(r^2\). Circumference is a length, so its radius isn’t squared.









TipHint 2





The diameter is two radii long, so the formula for \(d\) has a 2 in it. The equation of a circle is the only one with both \(x\) and \(y\).








Name
Formula




Area of a circle
\(A = \pi r^2\)


Circumference
\(C = 2\pi r\)


Diameter
\(d = 2r\)


Equation of a circle
\((x-h)^2 + (y-k)^2 = r^2\)
